newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen up on carryover, near 5,000 pts.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen up on carryover, near 5,000 pts.

text.p: --Mexico stocks seen up on follow-through, long bond
--Peso likely weak on dollar put auction
Dealers saw stocks extending their record advance at the open on Thursday on strong momentum from the previous session with buyers lured by U.S. 30-year Treaaury bonds, up 8/32 to yield 6.31 percent.
"It seems incredible after yesterday's huge gains, but buying shows few signs of letting up," one desk trader said.
Technical analysts placed resistance for the IPC scale at 5,000 points. Thursday's record close was at 4,974.23 points.

Traders said the peso was likely to open weak on demand for dollars to participate in the central bank's dollar put auction later in the day. Banco de Mexico announced Wednesday it would auction $500 million rather than the usual $300 million in puts.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.8000/7.8500 per dollar for the 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.8000/7.8200 per dollar, compared to Wednesday's close of 7.7825/7.7900.
Overnight rates on Cetes were seen opening near the prior close of 17.50 percent.
